title: Encore: Why you should aim to be a “good enough” parent, with Tim Cavell, PhD, and Lauren Quetsch, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a summer break, so we're rerunning some of our favorite episodes from the paSt. In 2023, I talked to psychologists Tim Cavell and Lauren Quetch
sentences.zh: 《心理学话你知》正在度过暑假，因此我们将重播过去一些备受喜爱的节目。在2023年，我与心理学家蒂姆·卡韦尔和劳伦·奎奇进行了交谈

sentences.en: about why parenting expectations seem higher than ever and how parents can focus on what really matters moSt. I hope you enjoy this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 探讨了为什么育儿期望似乎比以往任何时候都高，以及父母如何专注于真正最重要的事情。希望大家喜欢这期档案节目。

sentences.en: We'll be back with new episodes beginning August 26th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在8月26日回归并推出新节目。

sentences.en: Raising children can be particularly challenging these days.
sentences.zh: 如今抚养孩子尤其具有挑战性。

sentences.en: There are dozens of books and articles offering competing answers to nearly every parenting question you might have.
sentences.zh: 有几十本书和文章为你的几乎每一个育儿问题提供相互矛盾的答案。

sentences.en: From how to get your baby to sleep, to how to help siblings get along, to how much screen time is too much, to whether to let your tween attend a sleepover.
sentences.zh: 从如何让婴儿入睡，到如何帮助兄弟姐妹相处，再到屏幕时间多少才算过多，以及是否让你的准少年参加留宿派对。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, every parenting decision you make, even the most mundane ones, can feel consequential.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你做的每一个育儿决定，甚至是那些最微不足道的决定，都会让人觉得影响重大。

sentences.en: It's no wonder that many parents feel tired, stressed, and unsure of whether they're doing a good job.
sentences.zh: 难怪许多父母感到疲惫、压力重重，并且不确定自己是否做得很好。

sentences.en: In a recent Pew Research Center survey, 47% of mothers and 34% of fathers said they felt
sentences.zh: 在皮尤研究中心最近的一项调查中，47%的母亲和34%的父亲表示

sentences.en: that parenting was tiring most or all of the time, and one-third of mothers and one-quarter of fathers felt it was stressful all or most of the time.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得育儿在大部分或所有时间都令人精疲力竭，三分之一的母亲和四分之一的父亲觉得在所有或大部分时间都充满压力。

sentences.en: So as a parent, how do you know which of your choices matter most and where to focus your limited parenting energy?
sentences.zh: 因此，作为父母，你如何知道哪些选择最重要，又该把有限的育儿精力集中在哪里？

sentences.en: What's the right balance between keeping kids safe and giving them freedom?
sentences.zh: 在保护孩子安全与给予他们自由之间，什么是正确的平衡？

sentences.en: How should you respond when your kids try your patience with whining, sibling fights, or teenage sarcasm?
sentences.zh: 当孩子用唠叨、兄弟姐妹争吵或十几岁的讽刺来考验你的耐心时，你应该如何回应？

sentences.en: How should your parenting change as your kids get older?
sentences.zh: 随着孩子长大，你的育儿方式应该如何改变？

sentences.en: And most important, how can you develop a loving, supportive relationship with your children that will stand the test of time and lead to a happy, well-adjusted family?
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，你如何才能与孩子建立一种充满爱意、支持性的关系，经受住时间的考验，并建立一个幸福、适应良好的家庭？

sentences.zh: 我们今天的第二位嘉宾是

sentences.en: practical science-based strategies to build healthy and lasting parent-child relationships.

sentences.en: Let's start with the title of the book and why you chose it.
sentences.zh: 让我们从书名以及你们为什么选择这个名字开始。

sentences.en: What does it mean to be a good enough parent and why should parents aim for good enough as opposed to spectacular or out of this world?
sentences.zh: 做一个“足够好”的父母意味着什么？为什么父母应该追求“足够好”，而不是追求壮观或无与伦比？

sentences.en: We must concede that the term was borrowed.
sentences.zh: 我们必须承认这个术语是借用来的。

sentences.en: The phrase good enough mother was coined back in the
sentences.zh: “足够好的母亲”这个短语是由

sentences.en: 50s by a psychologist named Donald Winnicott, and the phrase good enough parenting has been around for quite a while.
sentences.zh: 50年代一位名叫唐纳德·温尼科特的心理学家创造的，“足够好的育儿”这个短语已经存在相当一段时间了。

sentences.en: In fact, you could probably find two or three books with similar titles that might invoke the term good enough or good enough parenting.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你大概能找到两三本书名相似的书，它们可能会用到“足够好”或“足够好的育儿”这个词。

sentences.en: It's interesting if you look at the history of
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾

sentences.en: Winnicott's use of the term because he thought that the perfect parent was less effective than the good enough parent.
sentences.zh: 温尼科特对这个词的使用历史，会发现这很有趣，因为他认为完美的父母不如足够好的父母有效。

sentences.en: And what he meant by that was that the good enough parent doesn't always meet every child's need.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是，足够好的父母并不总是能满足孩子的每一个需求。

sentences.en: In fact, he used the term fail.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他用了“失败”这个词。

sentences.en: Sometimes they fail to meet their child's every need.
sentences.zh: 有时他们未能满足孩子的所有需求。

sentences.en: And in so doing, children learn to cope on their own.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，孩子们学会了自己应对。

sentences.en: And we think that's an important message for today's parent because there's tons of information.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这对当今的父母来说是一个重要的信息，因为信息实在太多了。

sentences.en: To me, it feels like a weight to try to be a good parent.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，努力做一个好父母感觉像是一种沉重的负担。

sentences.en: It seems that if the bar has been set to perfect or at least quote unquote effective, and we wanted to write a book that describes in a more holistic fashion what it means
sentences.zh: 似乎标准已经被设定为完美，或者至少是所谓的“有效”，而我们想写一本书，以更全面的方式描述

sentences.en: to be a parent that's going to do what matters most and not wear yourself out in the process or not become a hyper hover parent as well.
sentences.zh: 做一个能做最重要事情的父母意味着什么，并且在这个过程中不会让自己筋疲力尽，或者不会变成一个过度盘旋的直升机父母。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think when we were talking about this and trying to decide on this title as well, you know, I have four young kids and one of the things that I've been involved
sentences.zh: 我想当我们讨论这个问题并试图决定这个书名时，你知道的，我有四个年幼的孩子，我所参与的事情之一

sentences.en: in, I have, there's a group of a few mothers that graduated from my PhD program and we all sort of lean on each other for parenting advice, if you will.
sentences.zh: 是，我有一个由几位从我的博士项目毕业的母亲组成的小组，如果可以的话，我们都会在育儿建议上互相依靠。

sentences.en: And what ends up happening, what I, what I've realized is a lot of what can be consumed about parenting is set, sets the bar really high to the point of
sentences.zh: 结果就是，我所意识到的是，关于育儿可以吸收的大量内容，把标准拉得非常高，高到这种地步

sentences.en: if I do something wrong, what does that mean for my child?
sentences.zh: 如果我做错了什么，这对我的孩子意味着什么？

sentences.en: My child is going to fail in life.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子将在生活中失败。

sentences.en: And this
sentences.zh: 而这

sentences.en: I've noticed has create, uh, created a really high amount of anxiety for new parents, um, in this generation.
sentences.zh: 我注意到已经产生，呃，为这一代的新父母创造了极高的焦虑感，嗯。

sentences.en: And I think, uh, it has really helped to talk to them and sort of bounce ideas off of each
sentences.zh: 我认为，嗯，与他们交谈并互相碰撞想法真的很有帮助

sentences.en: other, but also recognize that some of the things that we say are, you know, really important, like, well, you know, how does my kid look today?
sentences.zh: 彼此，但也认识到我们所说的一些事情是，你知道的，真的很重要，比如，嗯，“我的孩子今天看起来怎么样？”

sentences.en: Or, uh, maybe did I not handle this situation exactly right?
sentences.zh: 或者，呃，“我处理这个情况是不是没有完全正确？”

sentences.en: Comes down to, well, sometimes it's okay to just be good enough because if we worry too much
sentences.zh: 归结起来就是，有时只是“足够好”也没关系，因为如果我们过于担心

sentences.en: about all of the fine details, um, kind of like what was Tim was talking about is we, we miss the,
sentences.zh: 所有那些微小的细节，嗯，有点像蒂姆刚才谈到的那样，我们会错过

sentences.en: the larger picture of what it means to be a parent and what it means to, to run a family.
sentences.zh: 作为父母意味着什么以及经营一个家庭意味着什么的宏观图景。

sentences.en: And so good enough, I think is often now the advice that parents need more than ever, because they're told so many things about, you have to be this way.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为“足够好”现在往往是父母比以往任何时候都更需要的建议，因为他们被告知了太多事情，你必须这样。

sentences.en: And a perfect parent looks like this and it's just too much.
sentences.zh: 而一个完美的父母看起来是这样的，这实在是太多了。

sentences.en: It's too much to manage.
sentences.zh: 这太难以应付了。

sentences.en: Can I add to that?
sentences.zh: 我可以补充一点吗？

sentences.en: Because I agree wholeheartedly with what Lauren said.
sentences.zh: 因为我完全同意劳伦所说的话。

sentences.en: And, and I think our book aims for a sweet spot between, you know, there's one kind of parenting book that's a rather folksy, homespun approach to parenting.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为我们的书旨在寻找一个绝佳的平衡点，你知道，有一种育儿书是相当具有民间风味的育儿方法。

sentences.en: It's more of a literary work than a reflection of the science of parenting.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一部文学作品，而不是育儿科学的反映。

sentences.en: And then there are those books that are drawn tightly from the science of parenting, parenting, but those can get rather prescriptive and exacting.
sentences.zh: 还有那些紧密汲取育儿科学的书籍，但那些可能会变得相当教条和严苛。

sentences.en: And, and we were, our book I think is aimed sort of between the two at a, at a sweet spot, which says let, let's build from, let's draw
sentences.zh: 而且，我们的书我认为旨在两者之间的一个绝佳平衡点，它说，让我们从

sentences.en: from the science of parenting, but let's render it in a way that's user-friendly, that's parent-friendly, that's digestible.
sentences.zh: 育儿科学中汲取，但要以一种用户友好、父母友好、易于消化吸收的方式呈现出来。

sentences.en: And that distills this, the, the, the key findings down to an essential whole to what matters moSt.
sentences.zh: 并将这些关键发现提炼成一个核心整体，直指最重要的事情。

sentences.en: LESLIE KENDRICK Does the good enough approach in effect also extend to the kids?
sentences.zh: 这种“足够好”的方法实际上是否也适用于孩子们？

sentences.en: Because you know, there's so much pressure on our children these days to be absolutely perfect and spectacular.
sentences.zh: 因为你知道，现在我们的孩子面临着巨大的压力，要做到绝对完美和出色。

sentences.en: So if you're a good enough parent, well, maybe you can be a good enough son or daughter as well.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一个足够好的父母，嗯，也许你也可以做一个足够好的儿子或女儿。

sentences.en: LESLIE KENDRICK Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: I think sometimes people don't realize that when you set standards really high for yourself or for your child, like I want my child to be the greatest athlete there ever was.
sentences.zh: 我想有时人们没有意识到，当你为自己或你的孩子设定极高的标准时，比如我希望我的孩子成为有史以来最伟大的运动员。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And now I know what it means.
sentences.zh: 现在我知道这意味着什么了。

sentences.en: I mean, that means they need to be involved in three sports that take up all their time and the AP classes,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这意味着他们需要参加三项占用他们所有时间的运动以及大学先修课程（AP课程），

sentences.en: they need to be involved in all of those because my child's going to be the beSt.
sentences.zh: 他们需要参与所有这些，因为我的孩子要成为最棒的。

sentences.en: LESLIE KENDRICK And what ends up happening is
sentences.zh: 而最终发生的情况是

sentences.en: the child gets burnt out, the parent can get burnt out.
sentences.zh: 孩子精疲力竭，父母也可能会精疲力竭。

sentences.en: And when you base your family and your relationship off of those accomplishments, rather than the relationship you actually have with one another, you lose something in there.
sentences.zh: 当你把你的家庭和关系建立在那些成就之上，而不是你们实际彼此拥有的关系上时，你在其中就失去了某些东西。

sentences.en: And that can cause more distress rather than just focusing on, again, what matters most, the good enough.
sentences.zh: 这会带来更多的痛苦，而不是仅仅专注于——再次强调——最重要的事情，即“足够好”。

sentences.en: LESLIE KENDRICK Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think it's been way overstated that our parenting shapes our children and their personality and their future.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，我们的育儿方式塑造了我们的孩子、他们的性格和他们的未来，这种说法被大大夸大了。

sentences.en: There are a lot of other factors besides parenting practices that shape who children become.
sentences.zh: 除了育儿实践之外，还有许多其他因素塑造了孩子们成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: And more recent research speaks loudly to that.
sentences.zh: 最近的研究有力地说明了这一点。

sentences.en: And as a parent, my tendency is to adopt a posture of discovery.
sentences.zh: 作为父母，我的倾向是采取一种发现的姿态。

sentences.en: Let me discover who my children will become and let me be ready to love and accept them when I discover who they are.
sentences.zh: 让我去发现我的孩子将成为什么样的人，当我发现他们是谁时，让我准备好去爱他们并接受他们。

sentences.en: But the notion that I'm exercising my preferences and shaping who they are and who they become is both mythical and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 但那种认为我正在行使自己的偏好并塑造他们是谁以及他们将成为什么样的人的观点，既是神话又是危险的。

sentences.en: So it's an interesting posture to adopt, but I think it's a healthy one.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种有趣的姿态，但我认为它是健康的。

sentences.en: Let me learn who my child is.
sentences.zh: 让我去了解我的孩子是谁。

sentences.en: Let me learn who my child will become.
sentences.zh: 让我去了解我的孩子将成为谁。

sentences.en: And let me practice accepting who that child is and conveying a message of love and belonging.
sentences.zh: 让我练习接受那个孩子是谁，并传达爱与归属的信息。

sentences.en: That's a different way to go about the task of parenting.
sentences.zh: 这是进行育儿任务的一种不同方式。

sentences.en: LESLIE KENDRICK And I think that that segues into the question that I had, where you write about the most important job that parents have is to build a relationship with their
sentences.zh: 我想这顺理成章地引出了我的问题，你在书中写道，父母最重要的工作是与孩子建立

sentences.en: children.
sentences.zh: 关系。

sentences.en: And I think that might surprise some people maybe who don't think that they need to build a relationship because they have a relationship.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能会让某些人感到惊讶，他们可能认为自己不需要建立关系，因为他们已经有了关系。

sentences.en: But what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 但你们是什么意思？

sentences.en: What is the special approach that you recommend that might not be immediately evident to a harried mother or father?
sentences.zh: 你们推荐的这种特殊方法是什么？对于焦头烂额的父亲或母亲来说，这可能不是一眼就能看出来的。

sentences.en: LESLIE KENDRICK So I believe that we've got core components that we highlight within this book.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信我们在本书中强调了一些核心组成部分。

sentences.en: There are three aspects that we believe are really important for a relationship between a parent and a child.
sentences.zh: 有三个方面我们认为对父母与孩子之间的关系非常重要。

sentences.en: And then we also have some components that we feel are sort of the foundations of those things, too.
sentences.zh: 然后我们也有一些组成部分，我们觉得它们也是这些东西的基础。

sentences.en: So largely, when we're thinking about a relationship, which Tim alluded to already previously, was this posture of acceptance.
sentences.zh: 所以很大程度上，当我们考虑关系时——蒂姆之前已经提到过——就是这种接纳的姿态。

sentences.en: So when we think about
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们思考

sentences.en: our relationship with our child, we're really saying, I see you, and I accept who you are for who you are, right?
sentences.zh: 我们与孩子关系时，我们实际上是在说：我看到你了，我接纳本来的你，对吧？

sentences.en: So I have four little children, and I may parent them pretty similarly.
sentences.zh: 所以我有四个小孩子，我对他们的育儿方式可能相当相似。

sentences.en: You know, all close in age together as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，年龄也很接近。

sentences.en: And they are different.
sentences.zh: 但他们是不同的。

sentences.en: They're different people.
sentences.zh: 他们是不同的人。

sentences.en: They have different interests.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的兴趣。

sentences.en: They have different inclinations.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的倾向。

sentences.en: They have different temperaments.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的气质。

sentences.en: And so part of being a parent then is first saying, I see that you are who you are, and I'm okay with that.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为父母的一部分工作，首先是说：我看到你就是你，我对此没意见。

sentences.en: And that can look in many different ways.
sentences.zh: 这可以有很多不同的表现形式。

sentences.en: It can be very outward in the way that we express that.
sentences.zh: 在我们表达这一点的方式上，它可以非常外在。

sentences.en: And it can also be more silent in the way that we express that, too.
sentences.zh: 在我们表达这一点的方式上，它也可以更加无声。

sentences.en: So sometimes not saying anything and rather than correcting your child all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以有时什么也不说，而不是一直纠正你的孩子。

sentences.en: The second component of that then is containing.
sentences.zh: 第二个组成部分就是包容（containing）。

sentences.en: So thinking about our job as a parent is also to recognize that we, you know, children are impulsive sometimes.
sentences.zh: 因此，认为我们作为父母的工作也是要认识到，我们，你知道，孩子们有时是冲动的。

sentences.en: We still have to welcome them into the culture and society in which we live and and tell them what is and is not acceptable.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然必须欢迎他们融入我们生活的文化和社会中，并告诉他们什么是可以接受的，什么是不可以接受的。

sentences.en: And so our practices of containment sort of help us do that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们的包容实践在某种程度上有助于我们做到这一点。

sentences.en: And then the last component within that is being a leader and your leadership within the family.
sentences.zh: 然后其中的最后一个组成部分是成为领导者以及你在家庭中的领导力。

sentences.en: So outwardly expressing what it means to be a good person, talking about what our values are within a family.
sentences.zh: 也就是向外表达成为一个好人意味着什么，谈论我们在家庭中的价值观是什么。

sentences.en: And then sharing that with our children, too.
sentences.zh: 然后也与我们的孩子分享这一点。

sentences.en: There's more to that.
sentences.zh: 还有更多内容。

sentences.en: And I'll let Tim take over.
sentences.zh: 我让蒂姆接着讲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think if we zoom back a little bit, I think there needs to be an appreciation that
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们把镜头稍微拉远一点，我认为需要有一种认识，即

sentences.en: we have cast, we being mainly professionals like Lauren and I have tended to cast parenting as something set apart from relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们已经将——我们主要是指像劳伦和我这样的专业人士——把育儿归类为独立于关系之外的事情。

sentences.en: There are some parenting advice that's like an itemized list of if your child does X, you should do Y.
sentences.zh: 有些育儿建议就像是一份逐项列出的清单：如果你的孩子做了X，你就应该做Y。

sentences.en: If your child has this problem or engages in this behavior, and this is how you should respond without appreciating the context of the relationship in which those events occur.
sentences.zh: 如果你的孩子有这个问题或从事这种行为，这就是你应该如何回应的方式，却没有考虑到这些事件发生的关系背景。

sentences.en: You know, depending on how strong or strained the relationship is, you might want to do very different things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，根据关系的牢固或紧张程度，你可能想做非常不同的事情。

sentences.en: Because at the end of the day, it's the relationship that will move your child toward being a good, healthy citizen.
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，是这种关系会促使你的孩子成为一个优秀、健康的公民。

sentences.en: And I tend to say it this way, Kim, if there was some farcical choice I had to make between two surrogate parents, one who was very good at relationships in his or her
sentences.zh: 我倾向于这样说，金，如果我必须在两个代孕父母之间做出某种荒谬的选择，一个是他或她的人生中非常擅长处理关系的人

sentences.en: life, and one who knew a lot about parenting, I would choose the one who was good at relationships.
sentences.zh: 而另一个是对育儿知之甚多的人，我会选择那个擅长处理关系的人。

sentences.en: Because that's what it is.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是本质所在。

sentences.en: But too often, I think because of people like us throwing out so much advice, folks become parents and they move into this mode where they sort of jettison what they
sentences.zh: 但通常情况下，我认为由于像我们这样的人抛出了太多的建议，人们成为父母后，就会进入这样一种模式：他们抛弃了

sentences.en: think about in terms of how to make a relationship work.
sentences.zh: 他们关于如何让关系运作的想法。

sentences.en: None of the relationships we have should involve being victimized, taken advantage of, being abused.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的任何关系都不应涉及被 victimization（受害）、被利用、被虐待。

sentences.en: None of the relationships we have should involve not trying to convey a message of acceptance to the people we love and care about.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的任何关系都不应涉及不对我们所爱和关心的的人传达接纳的信息。

sentences.en: And none of the relationships we have should involve abandoning what our core values are, how we carry ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的任何关系都不应涉及放弃我们的核心价值观以及我们的行事方式。

sentences.en: So you want to bring all those relationship components to the parent-child relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以你想把所有这些关系的组成部分带入亲子关系中。

sentences.en: Not just because it's a parent-child relationship, because that's what it means to have a healthy relationship.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为这是一种亲子关系，更是因为这才是健康关系应有的意义。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the book, you ask parents to think about their parenting goals, which are not the same as the goals that they might have for their children's future.
sentences.zh: 在书的开头，你让父母思考他们的育儿目标，这与他们可能对孩子未来抱有的期望并不一样。

sentences.en: What do you mean when you talk about parenting goals?
sentences.zh: 你所说的育儿目标是什么意思？

sentences.en: How should parents set them and how can they stick to them?
sentences.zh: 父母应该如何设定目标，又该如何坚持下去？

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: We describe parenting goals as the goals parents have for guiding their parenting behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们将育儿目标描述为父母用来指导自身育儿行为的目标。

sentences.en: But it's seldom a topic of discussion.
sentences.zh: 但这很少成为被讨论的话题。

sentences.en: What are your parenting goals?
sentences.zh: 你的育儿目标是什么？

sentences.en: Again, we tend to think of it in terms of what we want for our children downstream.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们往往会从长远来看我们对孩子的期望去思考这个问题。

sentences.en: But if you, a parent, a working parent, you go home that evening, you have some goals in mind as a parent.
sentences.zh: 但如果你——一个父母，一个上班族父母——那天傍晚回到家，你作为父母心里其实是有一些目标的。

sentences.en: Oftentimes, they're sort of hidden and maybe embedded in automatic reactions to children.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，这些目标是某种程度上隐藏着的，也许内化在了对孩子的本能反应中。

sentences.en: Things become sort of mindless and routine.
sentences.zh: 事情变得有些盲目且流于形式。

sentences.en: And we may not be forward-thinking or conscious about, what are we trying to do in these interactions I have with my child?
sentences.zh: 而且我们可能不会有长远眼光，也没有意识到：在我们与孩子的这些互动中，我们到底想做什么？

sentences.en: And if there's value in having a relationship where children feel accepted, they are periodically contained.
sentences.zh: 如果让孩子感受到被接纳同时又定期受到约束的关系是有价值的，

sentences.en: In other words, there's a message of this you cannot do, and the parent is carrying
sentences.zh: 换句话说，传递出“这事你不能做”的信息，并且父母行事的

sentences.en: himself or herself in a way that espouses good values, then those are great goals to guide parenting behavior.
sentences.zh: 方式践行着良好的价值观，那么这些就是指导育儿行为的极佳目标。

sentences.en: Now, will you know the outcome immediately in terms of your children's functioning?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能立即从孩子的表现中看到结果吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: It's like a plan.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一项计划。

sentences.en: It takes time for that to unfold.
sentences.zh: 成果显现需要时间。

sentences.en: So, the goals for parenting behavior are more proximal to what we do in any given day or situation.
sentences.zh: 因此，育儿行为的目标与我们在任何特定日子或情况下的实际做法更加贴近。

sentences.en: And to add on that too, when we act automatically, we may be doing ourselves harm in that relationship.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，当我们出于本能行事时，我们可能正在损害我们与孩子之间的关系。

sentences.en: And so, thinking about our goal as
sentences.zh: 因此，把我们的目标设定为

sentences.en: just having a stronger relationship with our child rather than worrying about who they're going to be or are they the smartest kid in the class?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是与孩子建立更深厚的关系，而不是去担忧他们将来会成为什么样的人、是不是班里最聪明的孩子，

sentences.en: Are they the best athlete?
sentences.zh: 是不是最好的运动员？

sentences.en: Are they the best dressed?
sentences.zh: 是不是穿得最好看？

sentences.en: Are they going to be X, Y, and Z?
sentences.zh: 他们会不会达成这样那样的成就？

sentences.en: That may snap in as an automatic goal that you're not thinking about where you're snarky with your kid or you're telling them what they need to be doing.
sentences.zh: 那些担忧可能会突然变成一种你并未意识到的本能目标，导致你对孩子冷嘲热讽，或者对他们指手画脚。

sentences.en: And that sort of forces your hand sometimes to say, how hard am I going to push?
sentences.zh: 这有时会逼得你不得不去想：我到底要逼他们到什么程度？

sentences.en: If my kid isn't doing what I want them to do right now, I may be pushing an agenda I'm not even aware of consciously at the expense of the relationship that I have with my child.
sentences.zh: 如果我的孩子现在不按我的意愿行事，我可能在以牺牲我和孩子之间的关系为代价，去推进一个连我自己都没有意识到的计划。

sentences.en: And so, if my goal is, maybe I'm struggling with the relationship with my child right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我的目标是——也许我现在正苦恼于和孩子的关系。

sentences.en: So, if my goal, if I'm conscious about, I care about my child feeling loved and wanting them to love me back too.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我的目标是有意识的，我在意的是让孩子觉得自己被爱，并希望他们也同样爱我。

sentences.en: And obviously, you can't make your child do anything in that way.
sentences.zh: 显然，你没法强迫你的孩子以那种方式做任何事。

sentences.en: You can't force them to love you.
sentences.zh: 你无法强迫他们爱你。

sentences.en: And yet, if you have that goal of, I want us to be stronger together and you're more thoughtful about it, that can change how you act in a moment.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你怀揣着“我想让我们共同变得更好”这个目标，并且考虑得更周到，这就能改变你在某个时刻的行事方式。

sentences.en: And so, cleaning up the floor or addressing the tone in which they spoke back to you may seem like that's the most important thing if we're thinking automatically in that moment.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们当时出于本能思考，收拾地板或者纠正他们顶嘴的语气，可能会显得是最重要的事情。

sentences.en: But if we say, my relationship is the most important, our relationship together is the most important, then maybe you let some of those things go.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们说，我的关系最重要，我们彼此的关系最重要，那么你也许就会对其中的某些事情释怀。

sentences.en: And that actually ends up building that relationship stronger.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上最终会巩固并加深这种关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's being intentional, deliberate, and explicit with why you're doing what you're doing
sentences.zh: 作为父母，这要求你对自己的所作所为保持有意识、刻意且明确的动机，

sentences.en: as a parent as opposed to reacting out of some hidden emotional goal, like I'm frustrated or I'm tired,
sentences.zh: 而不是出于某种隐藏的情绪化目标做出反应，比如感到沮丧或疲惫，

sentences.en: or out of some preference to live vicariously through your child.
sentences.zh: 或者出于想要将自己的人生寄托在孩子身上的某种偏好。

sentences.en: And we offer to parents that useful goals to keep in mind are conveying a message of acceptance, conveying a message of containment,
sentences.zh: 我们向父母建议，值得牢记的实用目标是：传达接纳的信息、传达约束的信息——

sentences.en: that there are some things you cannot do, and then conveying a message of what our family values, what we believe in and hold dear.
sentences.zh: 即有些事是不能做的——然后传达我们家庭的价值观、我们所信仰和珍视的东西是什么的信息。

sentences.en: So, let me pick up from what you've just said, because you're talking about containment rather than discipline.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我接着你刚才的话往下说，因为你谈到的是“约束”而不是“管教”。

sentences.en: And in the book, you offer a rule of thumb.
sentences.zh: 在书中，你提出了一个经验法则。

sentences.en: You call it the 80-20 rule.
sentences.zh: 你称之为“八二法则”。

sentences.en: What is that and how does that work?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: So, we make the provocative point that effective discipline is selective discipline.
sentences.zh: 我们提出了一个带有启发性的观点：有效的管教是有选择性的管教。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, there's a lot of science on inept, what Jerry Patterson and colleagues at Oregon
sentences.zh: 关于不当管教，有很多科学研究。杰里·帕特森（Jerry Patterson）及俄勒冈

sentences.en: Social Learning Center used to call inept discipline with children whose behavior was disruptive and defiant.
sentences.zh: 社会学习中心的同事们过去常常用这个词来形容针对行为具有破坏性和挑衅性儿童的不当管教。

sentences.en: And the pattern that was observed in these parents was of two sorts, either being quite harsh and overly punitive or being quite lax and permissive.
sentences.zh: 在这些父母身上观察到的模式大致有两种：要么相当严厉和过度惩罚，要么相当松懈和纵容。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Not unlike, you know,
sentences.zh: 这不难让人想起，你知道的，

sentences.en: Balmerin's distinction.
sentences.zh: 鲍姆林德（Baumrind）的分类。

sentences.en: So, and it makes sense if you're a parent who's having trouble controlling your child's behavior, then you might wax and wane between being permissive and harsh,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你是一个在控制孩子行为方面遇到困难的父母，这种现象是合乎逻辑的：你可能会在纵容和严厉之间反复摇摆，

sentences.en: harsh and permissive.
sentences.zh: 一会儿严厉，一会儿纵容。

sentences.en: And so, it can be countered by having clarity about, well, what are the things that matter most?
sentences.zh: 而要解决这个问题，可以通过明确以下几点来应对：到底什么才是最重要的事情？

sentences.en: What are the things that you want to be consistent on in terms of being a disciplinarian?
sentences.zh: 在扮演管教者角色时，你希望在哪些事情上保持一致？

sentences.en: And what things do you let go?
sentences.zh: 又有哪些事情是你可以放任不管的？

sentences.en: Sometimes it's said in the parenting literature, Kim, is choose your battles wisely, right?
sentences.zh: 育儿文献中常说的一句话，金，就是“明智地选择你的战场”，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a very common phrase.
sentences.zh: 这是一句非常常见的俗语。

sentences.en: It's a bit unfortunate that the word battle is in there, but nonetheless, the point about choosing wisely is well founded.
sentences.zh: 里面带有“战场”这个词多少有点遗憾，不过无论如何，“明智选择”这个观点是很有道理的。

sentences.en: But it's not often talked about like, well, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 但人们往往不会去讨论：这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: You know, choose your battle wisely.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，“明智地选择你的战场”。

sentences.en: Well, we think that the science of parenting points us in a direction there in developmental psychology.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们认为发展心理学中的育儿科学为我们指明了方向。

sentences.en: One of the behaviors that is most problematic for children's development is their use of coercion, which is a broad term used
sentences.zh: 对儿童发展最具危害性的行为之一是他们对强制手段（coercion）的使用，这是一个广泛的术语，用来

sentences.en: to define various forms of aggression or antagonistic or threatening behavior.
sentences.zh: 定义各种形式的攻击性、对抗性或威胁性行为。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Children who learn to use coercion, aggression, and other sorts of antagonistic behavior are at risk for a lot of
sentences.zh: 学会使用强制手段、攻击行为以及其他对抗性行为的孩子，未来面临许多

sentences.en: problems downstream, school dropout, delinquency, substance use, things like that.
sentences.zh: 问题的风险很高，比如辍学、违法乱纪、滥用药物等等。

sentences.en: And so, clearly, this is a category that matters most, that matters a lot.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这属于最重要、影响极大的类别。

sentences.en: So, if you're looking for where to put your time and energy, it makes sense to put your time and energy on limiting your child's use of coercion and aggression.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在寻找应该把时间和精力花在哪里，那么把时间和精力放在限制孩子使用强制手段和攻击行为上是合情合理的。

sentences.en: Now, there are a whole host of other things that matter little to children's development.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有一大堆对儿童发展影响微乎其微的其他事情。

sentences.en: I think we give an example in the book of bacon eating.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在书中举过吃培根的例子。

sentences.en: You know, what if your daughter was eating bacon and only bacon?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你的女儿一直在吃培根，而且只吃培根呢？

sentences.en: And just it persisted and you said, well, you got to eat something else and that's all she ate.
sentences.zh: 并且这种行为持续下去，你对她说，你得吃点别的，可她还是只吃那个。

sentences.en: So, at what point does bacon eating rise to a significant problem?
sentences.zh: 那么，吃培根在什么时候会演变成一个严重的问题？

sentences.en: It might take a while before that's a significant problem or nose picking or whatever.
sentences.zh: 在它成为一个严重的问题之前可能需要很长时间，或者挖鼻孔之类的行为也一样。

sentences.en: There's a lot of things that we as parents can prefer that our children not do that we find maybe disgusting or
sentences.zh: 作为父母，我们可能会倾向于不希望孩子去做很多事情，我们可能会觉得这些事情令人厌恶、

sentences.en: unsightly or that it might be annoying.
sentences.zh: 不雅观，或者可能会很烦人。

sentences.en: But that's very different than saying this behavior, if repeated, has developmental significance.
sentences.zh: 但这与“这种行为如果重复发生，具有发展上的重要意义”完全是两码事。

sentences.en: There are not many of those to pay attention to, but the ones that aren't, you really want to pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 需要关注的事情并不多，但对于那些确实需要关注的，你真的必须予以重视。

sentences.en: And here's the kicker.
sentences.zh: 重头戏来了。

sentences.en: If you're going after, let's say, hypothetically, 20 different behaviors, only two of which matter,
sentences.zh: 假设、纯粹假设你要去管束20种不同的行为，其中只有2种是真正重要的，

sentences.en: and you're going to be spreading thin your efforts to discipline and contain and likely fail.
sentences.zh: 如果你把管教和约束的精力分散得太薄，大概率会以失败告终。

sentences.en: And so, you actually dilute your authority.
sentences.zh: 因此，你实际上是在削弱自己的权威。

sentences.en: You dilute the degree to which children see you as a person of authority because you're not being effective and because you're trying to do too much.
sentences.zh: 你削弱了孩子们将你视为权威人物的程度，因为你的做法不够有效，而且你试图管的事情太多了。

sentences.en: And so, you want to preserve your efforts at containment for things that matter moSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，你应当把你的约束精力留给那些最重要的事情。

sentences.en: We actually, some of my research looked at children's beliefs about whether parents and teachers can contain them if there's a conflict in goals.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我的一些研究探讨了儿童对于“如果在目标上发生冲突，父母和老师是否能够约束他们”的看法。

sentences.en: We had a measure and one of the items was something like, you want to go play outside.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一个测评，其中有一个题目类似于：你想去外面玩。

sentences.en: Your mom says, you can't go play outside.
sentences.zh: 你妈妈说，你不能去外面玩。

sentences.en: Can she make you stay inside?
sentences.zh: 她能让你留在家里吗？

sentences.en: So, it's an effort to get it.
sentences.zh: 这其实是在探究：

sentences.en: Do children believe that adults are in charge?
sentences.zh: 孩子们是否认为成年人说了算？

sentences.en: Well, lo and behold, most kids say, yes, they're in charge.
sentences.zh: 结果不出所料，大多数孩子都回答：是的，他们说了算。

sentences.en: But for the kids who doubt that, for the kids who have a low sense of containment, they had high levels of problem behavior, regardless of how well parents discipline.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些对此产生怀疑的孩子、那些约束感较低的孩子，无论父母管教得多么好，他们的问题行为发生率都很高。

sentences.en: So, if children are operating from a belief that I can outwit you, you know, do a turnaround and I can work around you, if they doubt your position of authority, that's not good.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果孩子们的行事逻辑是“我能难倒你，你知道的，转个头我就能糊弄过去”，如果他们对你的权威地位产生怀疑，那可不是什么好事。

sentences.en: And so, you want to protect and preserve your position of authority through the use of selective discipline.
sentences.zh: 所以，你要通过选择性管教来保护和维护你的权威地位。

sentences.en: The other win that comes from that is that you reduce the number of occasions where the interactions are emotionally negative because discipline can often
sentences.zh: 这样做带来的另一个好处是，你减少了互动中带有负面情绪的场合，因为管教往往

sentences.en: involve negative emotionality, unpleasant encounters.
sentences.zh: 会伴随着负面情绪和令人不愉快的遭遇。

sentences.en: So, if you reduce the occasions where you're trying to discipline your child to contain your child where there's negative emotions, then guess what happens?
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你减少了试图管教和约束孩子、进而产生负面情绪的场合，你猜会发生什么？

sentences.en: Your relationship is more positive than negative.
sentences.zh: 你们的关系就会呈现出积极多于消极的状态。

sentences.en: And again, there's pretty consistent research that shows that an 80% or about four to one ratio
sentences.zh: 同样，相当一致的研究表明，积极或中性的交流与消极交流的比例达到80%左右、

sentences.en: of positive or neutral exchanges to negative exchanges signals a satisfying, stable relationship.
sentences.zh: 也就是大约四比一时，标志着一种令人满意且稳定的关系。

sentences.en: If you're a parent who's at 50%, half the time it's negative, half the time it's positive, that's not good.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个处于50%比例的父母——一半时间是消极的，一半时间是积极的——那可不太妙。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And so, the goal would be to kind of use your gut as a barometer of how is my relationship with my child going?
sentences.zh: 所以，目标应该是把你的直觉当作一个晴雨表，来衡量我和孩子的关系进展如何？

sentences.en: Am I experiencing at least 80% or close to it of my interactions as neutral or positive?
sentences.zh: 我的互动中，是否至少有80%或者接近这个比例是中性或积极的？

sentences.en: And neutral is the key part of that.
sentences.zh: 其中，“中性”是关键的部分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It was like a coin flip.
sentences.zh: 就像抛硬币一样。

sentences.en: Like, I never know when we're going to be back in the relationship red.
sentences.zh: 就像是：我永远不知道我们什么时候又会回到充满火药味的紧张关系中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that was beautifully said, Tim.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆，你这话说得太美妙了。

sentences.en: And I think often when we give that figure, you know, it's gone from, it can be four to one, right, that these things are happening as well.
sentences.zh: 我想，当我们给出这个数据时，你知道的，它已经从……也可以是四比一，对吧，这些事情同样也在发生。

sentences.en: But I think people freak out because they say, how am I supposed to, you know, in a society, an American society where we're like, you got to be happy.
sentences.zh: 但我认为人们会惊慌失措，因为他们会说：我怎么能做到呢，你知道的，在一个要求你必须快乐的社会里，一个美国社会里。

sentences.en: And that's a sign of things working well, right?
sentences.zh: 而这也是事情运作良好的标志，对吧？

sentences.en: I think when we start
sentences.zh: 我认为当我们开始

sentences.en: providing the context of, well, you know, most of the time things should be happy, then I think that also sets up unrealistic expectations.
sentences.zh: 提供这样的背景时——“好吧，你知道的，大多数时候事情应该是快乐的”——我认为这也设定了不切实际的期望。

sentences.en: So, the important component of that is neutral.
sentences.zh: 因此，其中重要的组成部分是“中性”。

sentences.en: Neutral or positive, not in, and so that is in direct contrast with negative.
sentences.zh: 中性或积极，而不是消极，所以这与消极形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: So, if you're noticing that the most of the time or even half of the time you're getting into spats or your child is getting
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你发现大多数时候、甚至一半时候你们都在争吵，或者你的孩子对你感到

sentences.en: frustrated with you and angry with you, then that is usually a problem.
sentences.zh: 沮丧和生气，那么这通常就是一个问题。

sentences.en: But if it's neutral, neutral can be my kid just whined at me when I gave them something, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果是中性的呢？中性可以表现为：当我给孩子某种东西时，他们冲我发牢骚，对吧？

sentences.en: We can ignore that.
sentences.zh: 我们可以忽略这一点。

sentences.en: The idea is, what do we focus on and what do we care about?
sentences.zh: 核心理念是：我们把重点放在哪里？我们在意什么？

sentences.en: And so, Tim also was talking about, you know, when there's coercion, it could be lying, stealing, things that do lead to those problem behaviors later
sentences.zh: 所以蒂姆刚才也谈到了，你知道的，当存在强制行为时，可能是撒谎、偷窃，这些确实会导致以后那些问题行为，

sentences.en: on and are more concerning as we've seen.
sentences.zh: 并且正如我们所见，这些行为更令人担忧。

sentences.en: Those are the things that we call, you know, you have to get your butt off the couch for, right?
sentences.zh: 这些就是我们所说的，你知道的，你得从沙发上站起来去管的事，对吧？

sentences.en: Those are the things we don't ignore.
sentences.zh: 这些是我们不能忽视的事情。

sentences.en: Those are the things we have to stand up and we have to deal with that, that frustrating confrontation potentially.
sentences.zh: 这些是我们必须站出来、必须去处理的、可能充满挫败感的对峙事件。

sentences.en: For young kids, you know, they throw tantrums, they get really angry.
sentences.zh: 对于幼儿来说，你知道的，他们会发脾气，会非常生气。

sentences.en: I know that all too well.
sentences.zh: 这一点我再清楚不过了。

sentences.en: And recognizing those things are important.
sentences.zh: 认识到这些事情很重要。

sentences.en: And some things just aren't worth the time or the energy because it does sacrifice that relationship that you have with your child.
sentences.zh: 而有些事情根本不值得浪费时间和精力，因为这确实会牺牲你和孩子之间的关系。

sentences.en: So, do I like that my child rolled their eyes at me or, you know, was used a whiny voice or I just cooked dinner and now, and no, ugh, mom, that's gross.
sentences.zh: 所以，我会在意孩子对翻白眼吗？或者，你知道的，用了发牢骚的语气，或者我刚做好晚饭然后孩子说：“不，呃，妈妈，太恶心了。”

sentences.en: I get that a lot.
sentences.zh: 我经常遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's not worth fighting about, right?
sentences.zh: 有时候这不值得争吵，对吧？

sentences.en: You let it go, you let it slide.
sentences.zh: 你随它去，让它过去。

sentences.en: And it's to the benefit of the relationship because of that.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，这对维系关系是有好处的。

sentences.en: And an additional component to that is, you know, when you have a child that is really well behaving, right?
sentences.zh: 另一个相关的组成部分是，你知道的，当你有一个表现非常好的孩子时，对吧？

sentences.en: So, they're not lying.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不撒谎。

sentences.en: They're not getting into physical altercations with people.
sentences.zh: 他们不跟别人发生肢体冲突。

sentences.en: You can focus on some of that smaller stuff.
sentences.zh: 你就可以把精力放在一些比较小的事情上。

sentences.en: You know, if your kid listens to you, I don't know, young kids on average will listen six out of ten times.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你的孩子听话，平均来说，小孩子们在十次里会有六次听你的。

sentences.en: Really, really little kids, right?
sentences.zh: 非常非常小的孩子，对吧？

sentences.en: That's pretty good if they're listening six out of ten times.
sentences.zh: 如果他们十次里有六次听话，那已经相当不错了。

sentences.en: And often when kids come in that I've seen that have behavior problems, we're seeing zero out of ten times, two out of ten times, right?
sentences.zh: 通常当有行为问题的孩子来找我时，我们看到这种情况发生的概率是十分之零或十分之二，对吧？

sentences.en: And if you've got kids that are really pretty compliant, then you can, you know, you can start enforcing some things that maybe other parents
sentences.zh: 如果你遇到的孩子相当听话，那你就可以，你知道，开始强制执行一些可能其他父母

sentences.en: that have a more difficult relationship with their child cannot.
sentences.zh: 那些与孩子关系较难相处的父母所做不到的事情。

sentences.en: So, hey, I told you, you know, every time you leave a room, turn off the lights.
sentences.zh: 所以，嘿，我告诉过你，你知道，每次你离开房间时，把灯关掉。

sentences.en: Or we have this rule where you put your shoes by the front door.
sentences.zh: 或者我们有这样一个规则，把鞋子放在前门旁边。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: If your kid is a generally happy kid and your relationship is not continuously strained and they're not beating other kids up and lying, then those are the things you can focus on.
sentences.zh: 如果你的孩子总体上是个快乐的孩子，你们的关系也没有持续紧张，他们也没有殴打其他孩子或说谎，那么这些就是你可以关注的事情。

sentences.en: But if you've got a kid that you're having a really hard relationship with and they are lying, they are
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你和一个孩子的关系非常糟糕，而且他们在说谎，他们在

sentences.en: getting into a lot of fights, there's a lot of verbal issues going on where they're screaming at you,
sentences.zh: 卷入许多争吵中，有很多言语上的问题，他们对你大喊大叫，

sentences.en: those types of enforcement, those little things are what we should ignore.
sentences.zh: 那种强制执行，那些小事情才是我们应该忽略的。

sentences.en: So, it's a tiered system.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个分层系统。

sentences.en: And we talk about that more in the book, too.
sentences.zh: 我们在书中也更多地讨论了这一点。

sentences.en: I think that you talk about mindful and mindless parenting.
sentences.zh: 我想你们谈到了正念育儿与无意识育儿。

sentences.en: And I wanted to talk about the differences between the two, because I think that some of what you're talking about requires a level of mindfulness.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈这两者之间的区别，因为我认为你们所谈论的一些内容需要一定水平的正念。

sentences.en: But mindless parenting also has a role.
sentences.zh: 但无意识育儿也发挥着作用。

sentences.en: And I think, as you say, it's not because the parent is unplugged or inept.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，正如你们所说，这并不是因为父母不在线或无能。

sentences.en: But what are some examples of the two?
sentences.zh: 那么这两者有哪些例子呢？

sentences.en: And how can parents use those techniques to their advantage?
sentences.zh: 父母如何利用这些技巧来为自己谋取优势呢？

sentences.en: So, we don't use the word mindless to mean that someone's being stupid or unwise.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们使用“无意识”这个词并不是指某人愚蠢或不明智。

sentences.en: It's meant to imply a mental state in which you're operating on automatic, in an over-learned, automatic way.
sentences.zh: 它是用来暗示一种心理状态，在这种状态下，你是按自动驾驶模式运作的，是一种过度习得的、自动的方式。

sentences.en: So, you're not deliberate and conscious about what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于你正在做的事情，你并不是深思熟虑和有意识的。

sentences.en: Mindful parenting, on the other hand, involves a much more conscious, deliberate, effortful decision about what you're going to do.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，正念育儿涉及对你将要做的事情做出更有意识、深思熟虑、费力的决定。

sentences.en: We can't operate that way 24-7.
sentences.zh: 我们无法全天候以这种方式运作。

sentences.en: It's impossible, whether it's a parent or anyone.
sentences.zh: 这是不可能的，无论是对父母还是对任何人。

sentences.en: But you can move into that mode at times.
sentences.zh: 但你有时可以进入那种模式。

sentences.en: The danger is not appreciating that some of your parenting is rather mindless, automatic, and over-learned.
sentences.zh: 危险在于没有意识到你的一些育儿方式相当无意识、自动且过度习得。

sentences.en: And so, if you keep finding yourself stuck in the same old dynamic of getting crossways with your child, and you're both angry and frustrated and sad and hurt,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你发现自己总是陷入与孩子对立的同一种旧有动态中，并且你们两个都感到愤怒、沮丧、悲伤和受伤，

sentences.en: then you might want to consider the possibility that there's some automatic over-learned aspects to your parenting.
sentences.zh: 那么你可能需要考虑这样一种可能性，即你的育儿方式中存在一些自动的、过度习得的方面。

sentences.en: And it would be important to attend to what it is that you're feeling, experiencing, and thinking as you begin to engage or interact with your child.
sentences.zh: 当你开始与孩子接触或互动时，关注你的感受、体验和想法是很重要的。

sentences.en: So, we have an entire chapter in our book devoted to health.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们书中有整整一章专门讨论健康。

sentences.en: We see it as an essential ingredient in parenting, parents' health.
sentences.zh: 我们将健康——父母的健康——视为育儿中必不可少的要素。

sentences.en: And much of that is emotional health.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分是情绪健康。

sentences.en: And research in the last two decades has spoken very
sentences.zh: 过去二十年的研究非常

sentences.en: robustly to the fact that managing our emotional health requires that we can pause.
sentences.zh: 有力地证明了，管理我们的情绪健康需要我们能够暂停。

sentences.en: We can hit the pause button psychologically and attend to what's happening inside, what we're thinking,
sentences.zh: 我们可以在心理上按下暂停键，关注内心正在发生的事情，我们在想什么，

sentences.en: what we're feeling, as opposed to reacting rather quickly in an automatic over-learned way to get rid of whatever unpleasantness we're feeling.
sentences.zh: 我们的感受是什么，而不是以一种自动的、过度习得的方式相当迅速地做出反应，以摆脱我们感受到的任何不愉快。

sentences.en: Most people cope from the head down in that automatic over-learned way.
sentences.zh: 大多数人以那种自动且过度习得的方式从头部向下进行应对。

sentences.en: And we recommend coping, we call it from the ground up, getting grounded in the present
sentences.zh: 我们建议的应对方式，我们称之为从地面向上，立足于当下

sentences.en: moment, paying attention to what you're feeling, and then going to the head with a wise plan.
sentences.zh: 时刻，关注你的感受，然后带着明智的计划回到头部。

sentences.en: So, it's about being aware of, you know, awarenessing, as Kabat-Zinn, the person who brought
sentences.zh: 所以，这关乎觉察，你知道，正如卡巴金——将

sentences.en: mindfulness into healthcare would say, my awarenessing is biggest than thinking because it subsumes thinking.
sentences.zh: 正念引入医疗保健的人——所说的那样，我的觉察比思考更大，因为它包含了思考。

sentences.en: But a lot of parents don't practice being aware in a zoomed back fashion of what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 但许多父母并没有练习以一种抽离的方式去觉察他们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: So, none of this happens without practice, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，所有这些都不会凭空发生，都需要练习。

sentences.en: So, you can't just decide one day to be a mindful parent.
sentences.zh: 所以，你不能只凭一天决定成为一个正念父母。

sentences.en: It requires that you practice pausing, being in the moment, and leaning into what you're feeling.
sentences.zh: 这需要你练习暂停、身处当下，并倾听你的感受。

sentences.en: And we spent an entire chapter unpacking that.
sentences.zh: 我们花了一整章来剖析这一点。

sentences.en: Both of you work with kids who have serious behavior issues in your research and in your clinical work.
sentences.zh: 你们俩在研究和临床工作中都接触过有严重行为问题的儿童。

sentences.en: Is your advice different for those parents than it is for dealing with run-of-the-mill everyday problems?
sentences.zh: 对于这些父母，你们的建议与处理日常普通问题的建议不同吗？

sentences.en: Or does the same type of advice apply across the board for all types of families and situations?
sentences.zh: 还是说同样类型的建议适用于所有类型的家庭和情况？

sentences.en: And Dr. Quetch, maybe you could answer first based on your work with disruptive children and those who have autism spectrum disorder.
sentences.zh: Quetch 博士，也许你可以根据你对有破坏性行为的儿童以及自闭症谱系障碍儿童的研究，先回答这个问题。

sentences.en: A lot to unpack there, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想这里有很多内容需要剖析。

sentences.en: Because historically, a lot of the evidence-based treatments that we use to work with families to address disruptive behaviors assumes a lack of skill on the parent's side.
sentences.zh: 因为从历史上看，我们用来与家庭合作解决破坏性行为的许多循证疗法都假设父母缺乏技能。

sentences.en: So, often you will go to a treatment for your child who is experiencing disruptive behaviors and you'll go essentially so that a therapist can teach you possibly what
sentences.zh: 因此，通常情况下，当你的孩子出现破坏性行为时，你会去寻求治疗，而你去的本质上是为了让治疗师教导你可能

sentences.en: you're missing.
sentences.zh: 错过了什么。

sentences.en: It's assumed then, my child is misbehaving because of some sort of deficit within the parent.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们会假设，我的孩子行为不端是因为父母本身存在某种缺陷。

sentences.en: So, bad behavior on the child's part is sometimes assumed bad parenting, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，孩子不好的行为有时被认为是糟糕的育儿方式，对吧？

sentences.en: And we try to challenge that myth in a way because we say you can have skills and there may be other things getting
sentences.zh: 我们试图在某种程度上挑战这种神话，因为我们说你可以拥有技能，但可能还有其他事情在阻碍

sentences.en: in the way of you being able to connect with your child in a meaningful way.
sentences.zh: 你与孩子建立有意义的联系。

sentences.en: So, when working with parents of autistic kids, a lot of these parents do have great skills and they are challenged because they have a neurodivergent child.
sentences.zh: 因此，在与自闭症儿童的父母合作时，许多这样的父母确实拥有出色的技能，但他们面临挑战，因为他们有一个神经多样性的孩子。

sentences.en: They don't understand how their child experiences the world.
sentences.zh: 他们不理解他们的孩子是如何体验这个世界的。

sentences.en: And if they're neurotypical themselves, they think, well, when a child screams and throws a fit, that means they're being defiant, right?
sentences.zh: 如果他们自己是神经典型者，他们会想，嗯，当孩子尖叫并大发脾气时，这意味着他们在挑衅，对吧？

sentences.en: And therefore, I will approach my child as if they're being defiant and I handle it by providing, you know, there's a sanction or I put them in time
sentences.zh: 因此，我对待孩子的方式就像他们在挑衅一样，我通过提供，你知道的，实施制裁，或者让他们去罚站

sentences.en: out or I, you know, have privileges removed.
sentences.zh: 或者我，你知道的，剥夺特权来处理。

sentences.en: But it's different because sometimes a child is not tantruming because you've told them no, but instead they're having a meltdown
sentences.zh: 但这有所不同，因为有时孩子发脾气不是因为你对他们说了“不”，而是因为他们在经历精神崩溃

sentences.en: because they are overstimulated by their sensory overload in the environment, whether it's noise, light, touch.
sentences.zh: 由于他们在环境中受到感官过载的过度刺激，无论是噪音、光线还是触觉。

sentences.en: And so, to assume then your child is misbehaving because you lack skills is to neglect this complex, you know, child, this complex parent-child relationship in this environment
sentences.zh: 因此，如果认为你的孩子行为不端是因为你缺乏技能，那就是忽视了这种复杂的、你知道的孩子，这种复杂的亲子关系以及这种父母

sentences.en: that a parent may not even understand.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能无法理解的环境。

sentences.en: So, I think we frame it in a way in this book to understand what Tim had talked about earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为我们在本书中以某种方式来构建它，以理解 Tim 之前谈到的内容。

sentences.en: What are the behaviors that you're seeing and the more intense the behavior is such as lying, aggression, deceitfulness, we need to address that firSt.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的行为是什么，行为越强烈，例如说谎、攻击性、欺骗性，我们就需要首先解决这些问题。

sentences.en: And if those things are managed, then you sort of go up this funnel and these less intense behaviors, right, are something then that you can shift your parenting goals towards.
sentences.zh: 如果这些事情得到了控制，那么你就会沿着这个漏斗向上走，而这些不太强烈的行为，对吧，然后就可以成为你可以将育儿目标转移到的方向。

sentences.en: But it may look different for families based on their needs, based on the parent's own personal health, the family's health, other circumstances, difficult environments, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 但对于不同的家庭，根据他们的需求、父母个人的健康、家庭的健康、其他环境、困难的环境等，情况可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: So, yes, there are core things that we found to be really important to help sort of lead the child to success.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，有些核心的事情我们发现对于帮助引导孩子走向成功非常重要。

sentences.en: But to say one size fits all for each family or each parent-child relationship is neglecting the complexity of us as people and as a parent and a child together.
sentences.zh: 但如果说某种方法适用于每个家庭或每个亲子关系，那就是忽视了我们作为人以及父母与孩子在一起的复杂性。

sentences.en: Dr. Cavell, does that approach work when you're dealing with parents who have children who are bullies or may be bullied?
sentences.zh: Cavell 博士，当你处理那些孩子是霸凌者或可能是受欺凌者的父母时，这种方法管用吗？

sentences.en: I think the conditions necessary for a strong parent-child relationship are similar in terms of what's needed.
sentences.zh: 我认为建立牢固的亲子关系所需的条件在所需方面是相似的。

sentences.en: What's going to differ, Kim, is what's required of a parent depending on their child-rearing circumstances and the characteristic of the child.
sentences.zh: Kim，会有所不同的是，根据父母的抚养环境和孩子的特征，对父母的要求是什么。

sentences.en: I mean, the research is pretty clear that children arrive in this world with certain endowments, genetic endowments, which influences their environment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，研究非常清楚地表明，儿童带着某些天赋来到这个世界，基因天赋，这会影响他们的环境。

sentences.en: Some children are really easy to parent.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子很容易抚养。

sentences.en: Some children are very challenging to parent.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子抚养起来非常有挑战性。

sentences.en: And so, parents have to fit what they're doing to what their child needs.
sentences.zh: 因此，父母必须让他们所做的事情适应孩子的需求。

sentences.en: For children who are easy temperament, meet schedules, they're compliant, cooperative, they're emotionally regulated.
sentences.zh: 对于气质容易、适应时间表、听话、合作、情绪受调节的孩子。

sentences.en: Parenting, I think the parent-child relationship is going to have the same three conditions except contain and lead.
sentences.zh: 育儿，我认为亲子关系将具备相同的三个条件，除了包含和引导。

sentences.en: But parents won't have to work as hard as deliberately and it will be fairly easy to pull that off.
sentences.zh: 但父母不必像那样努力、有意识地工作，并且要做到这一点会相当容易。

sentences.en: When you have a challenging child, you have to be more intentional and conscious and explicit about what you're trying to do.
sentences.zh: 当你有一个具有挑战性的孩子时，你必须对你试图做的事情更有意图、更有意识、更明确。

sentences.en: Winnicott, who coined the term good enough mother, was a big fan of ordinary parents, ordinary mothers, in the sense that he saw in ordinary parents so many strengths.
sentences.zh: Winnicott 创造了“足够好的母亲”这个词，他是普通父母、普通母亲的忠实粉丝，因为他在普通父母身上看到了如此多的优势。

sentences.en: And I think our field over time has sort of cast parenting as extraordinary, as something, as a separate set of skills that you don't, you're not necessarily equipped
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的领域随着时间的推移把育儿塑造成了一种非凡的事情，作为某种你并不一定具备的

sentences.en: with, that you have to go to some book or some expert for.
sentences.zh: 独立技能集，你必须去读某本书或找某个专家。

sentences.en: We'd like to believe that if you can manage well your relationships, including the one with your child, you're going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 我们愿意相信，如果你能很好地管理你的人际关系，包括与孩子的关系，你就会过得很好。

sentences.en: But recognize that for some children, the task is going to be more challenging and it's going to look a little different.
sentences.zh: 但要认识到，对于某些孩子来说，这项任务将更具挑战性，并且看起来会有些不同。

sentences.en: Let's close with this one question.
sentences.zh: 让我们以这一个问题来结束。

sentences.en: I'm going to throw it at both of you sequentially, which is for each of you, what is one piece of parenting advice that you would like to leave with our listeners?
sentences.zh: 我将依次向你们两位提出这个问题，那就是对于你们每个人来说，有什么育儿建议是你想留给我们的听众的？

sentences.en: One of the things that I talk about within the beginning of the book, which when Tim approached me about writing this together, this is the first thing that came to my
sentences.zh: 我在书的开头谈论的一件事是，当 Tim 找我一起写这本书时，这是我脑海中浮现的第一件事，

sentences.en: mind and really stuck with me when I was first learning how to be a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始学习如何成为一名临床心理学家时，这深深地印在了我的脑海里。

sentences.en: So I'll give you this antidote and then I'll sort of end with what I mean by it all.
sentences.zh: 所以我先讲这个轶事，然后以我对这一切的理解来结束。

sentences.en: So I had a parent come in and she had a young boy and she leaned in close to me when she was trying to seek services and she said, I love my child, but I don't like my child.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有一位母亲带着一个小男孩来找我，当她试图寻求服务时，她靠我很近，她说：“我爱我的孩子，但我不喜欢我的孩子。”

sentences.en: And it stuck with me for so long and it took a long time for me to connect and understand what that meant finally when I had my children.
sentences.zh: 这件事在我脑海里停留了很久，直到我自己有了孩子，我花了很长时间才将其联系起来并最终理解了这意味着什么。

sentences.en: But I think the point being here that there are many things that you can work on as a parent.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这里的重点是，作为父母，有很多事情你可以努力去做。

sentences.en: We can always do better and seek for more for our children.
sentences.zh: 我们总能做得更好，为我们的孩子寻求更多。

sentences.en: And yet if we can lead with love and if we can remember that at the end of the day, our task is to love our children and be there for them and accept them.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我们能以爱引领，如果我们能记住，归根结底，我们的任务是爱我们的孩子，陪伴他们并接纳他们。

sentences.en: I think that is the biggest thing that needs to happen first before you worry about anything else.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是在担心其他任何事情之前最需要做的事情。

sentences.en: And so there are many things we want for our children.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对孩子有许多期望。

sentences.en: There are many things we hope for, for our children.
sentences.zh: 我们对孩子有许多希望。

sentences.en: And if we just can accept them for who they are and where they're at, I think that is the first, the first thing you have to accomplish as a parent before you can try
sentences.zh: 如果我们能完全按照他们的本来面目和他们所处的状态来接纳他们，我认为这是作为父母在尝试做其他事情之前必须完成的第一件事，

sentences.en: to do anything else.
sentences.zh: 第一件事。

sentences.en: Dr. Cavell?
sentences.zh: Cavell 博士？

sentences.en: Parenting involves the head and the heart or science and art, if you will.
sentences.zh: 育儿涉及头脑和心灵，或者可以说是科学与艺术。

sentences.en: And so some parents sometimes lead too much with what's happening emotionally.
sentences.zh: 所以有些父母有时在情绪发生的事情上投入过多。

sentences.en: And some parents are trying to do what the science they think is right.
sentences.zh: 有些父母则试图做他们认为是正确的科学。

sentences.en: The science tells us this, there are some things that are important and try to emphasize those things.
sentences.zh: 科学告诉我们这些，有些事情很重要，并试图强调这些事情。

sentences.en: And our book speaks to that.
sentences.zh: 我们的书也谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of things that are not, that don't matter that much.
sentences.zh: 有很多事情并不是这样，没有那么重要。

sentences.en: And so if you want to use your mind or the science of parenting, recognize that not everything is consequential.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你想运用你的头脑或育儿科学，请认识到并非每件事都有重大影响。

sentences.en: In fact, the science of parenting would say to you very strongly, when you go to decide where to put your energies, put it on the relationship.
sentences.zh: 事实上，育儿科学会非常强烈地告诉你，当你决定把精力放在哪里时，把它放在关系上。

sentences.en: That's where you double down.
sentences.zh: 那是你要加倍下注的地方。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And so if you're trying to decide, should I put my child in time?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在努力决定，我应该让我的孩子去罚站吗？

sentences.en: Not should I use a star chart?
sentences.zh: 不是我该用星星图吗？

sentences.en: Should I, you know, take him to a professional?
sentences.zh: 我应该，你知道的，带他去看专业人士吗？

sentences.en: Pay attention to the relationship.
sentences.zh: 关注这段关系。

sentences.en: Is my relationship with my child healthy?
sentences.zh: 我和孩子之间的关系健康吗？

sentences.en: Is it strong?
sentences.zh: 它牢固吗？

sentences.en: Has it, is it meeting that 80-20 criteria?
sentences.zh: 它是否符合那个 80-20 的标准？

sentences.en: And if not, what can I do to bolster that relationship?
sentences.zh: 如果没有，我能做些什么来巩固这段关系？

sentences.en: And I offer that because I don't think assessing the quality of the relationship is often what parents typically go to early.
sentences.zh: 我之所以提出这一点，是因为我认为评估关系的质量通常不是父母通常首先关注的。

sentences.en: Instead, they're looking for a quick answer to some, to fix some problem as opposed to saying, how are we doing my child and I?
sentences.zh: 相反，他们是在寻找一个快速的答案来解决某些问题，而不是说，我和我的孩子过得怎么样？

sentences.en: What can I do to make that relationship strong?
sentences.zh: 我能做些什么来让这段关系变得牢固？

sentences.en: Maybe do I need to, is it, does it need to be repaired in some way?
sentences.zh: 也许我需要，它是，它需要以某种方式修复吗？

sentences.en: Am I struggling emotionally to be available and patient with my child?
sentences.zh: 我在情感上是否很难对我的孩子保持包容和耐心？

sentences.en: What do I need to do to be an emotionally healthy parent so I can have a better relationship with my child?
sentences.zh: 我需要做些什么才能成为一个情感健康的父母，以便我和孩子能有更好的关系？

sentences.en: So it's, it's a different way to think about parenting, not as a job where you look at an endless series of fixes, but it's about a relationship that you manage
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种思考育儿的不同方式，不是把它当成一份你看不到尽头的修修补补的工作，而是把它当成一段你需要经营

sentences.en: 18 plus years.
sentences.zh: 18年以上的关系。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，我要感谢你们两位今天能来参加。

sentences.en: I think you have provided our listeners with some excellent and sound advice.
sentences.zh: 我认为你们为我们的听众提供了一些极好且稳妥的建议。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 别客气。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我们。
